title: Set a turn-end waiting mark from the Stop hook on every turn end
action:
Make the Stop hook record that control has returned to the human, on EVERY turn end (per D1). No text heuristic, no phrase table, no language detection — Stop itself is the signal.

WHERE IT HANGS. session_close/mod.rs's run_inner already discriminates the event: `event == "SessionEnd"` returns the native-only close path (near line 113) and `event == "PreCompact"` delegates (near line 119); everything else, Stop included, falls through to advisory() (near line 228). The existing Stop-only branch to copy the shape from is in nudges.rs, `maybe_bypass_block`, which opens `if ctx.event != "Stop" { return Ok(None); }` (near line 356). Search for these by their surrounding text; the line numbers are anchors and will drift.

WHAT TO WRITE (per D1, D3). When the event is Stop, set a waiting_on mark with kind `turn-end`. Reuse the existing store setters and the existing D3 target resolution in verbs/state_group/waiting_on.rs — session-scoped first, feature-scoped only when a feature is live. Do NOT add a second resolution path, and do NOT write the record directly: R128 keeps one seam onto the mark. The session id comes from reads.rs's get_session_id (near line 107); build_waiting_on requires a non-empty session, so a stop with no resolvable session id writes nothing rather than failing.

D5 — NEVER OVERWRITE. If a live mark already exists, leave it alone and write nothing. An agent that declared a gate or question wait this turn owns that mark; downgrading it to turn-end would erase exactly the distinction D3 exists to create. Check liveness with the existing waiting_on_is_live helper, not a fresh predicate.

D6 — THE SUBJECT. Use the last non-empty line of the turn's final assistant text block from the session transcript, trimmed and truncated. The transcript is already resolved and read on every Stop for the perf rollup — see resolve_transcript_for in session_close/perf.rs (near line 71) and rollup_transcript (near line 377). Reuse that resolution; do not add a second transcript read per turn. Transcript entries are JSONL; an assistant entry's message.content is an array whose blocks carry a `type`, and the text lives in the blocks with type `text` — the final assistant entry of a turn is often a tool_use with no text, so scan backwards for the last entry that actually has a text block. Pick the truncation length yourself (CONTEXT.md leaves it to your discretion); the constraint is that the result renders on ONE line in the session preamble and the compact capsule. build_waiting_on refuses an empty subject, so a turn whose final text is empty or whitespace-only still needs a non-empty fallback — choose one and say what it is in the trace.

BEST EFFORT, ALWAYS. A failed write is logged and the hook still emits its normal output; the Stop hook is never taken down by this. The shape to follow is already proven for the clearing path in hooks/prompt_context.rs — see clear_and_reap_waiting_on_best_effort (near line 338) and its failure-injection test.

Probe before guarding: check whether a re-entrant Stop (the payload's stop_hook_active flag, set when the turn is itself the continuation of a Stop hook that blocked) can double the mark. If it reproduces, guard it; if it cannot, say so in the trace and add no guard.

truths: A Stop event with no live mark writes a waiting_on mark whose kind is turn-end and whose subject is the transcript's last non-empty assistant text line
A live gate or question mark survives a Stop untouched (per D5)
SessionEnd, PreCompact, and any non-Stop event write no mark
A missing, unreadable, or malformed transcript leaves the Stop hook's normal output intact and writes no mark
A failing store write is logged and does not fail the Stop hook
A turn whose final text block is empty or whitespace-only still produces a non-empty subject

artifacts.substantive: a Stop-only branch that resolves the session, reads the transcript's last text line, and calls the existing waiting-on setter behind a live-mark check
cases for the happy path, the D5 no-overwrite rule, the non-Stop events, the empty-final-text fallback, and a failure injection proving the hook survives a failing write

key_links: the setter calls the store functions in verbs/state_group/waiting_on.rs, reusing their D3 target resolution rather than resolving the target again
the transcript path comes from session_close/perf.rs's existing resolver, so the hook still reads the transcript exactly once per turn
prohibitions: No second waiting_on writer and no second target resolver (per R128)
No provenance or source field on the mark (per D2)
No second transcript read per Stop
No text heuristic deciding whether the turn was a question (per D1)
The hook never overwrites a live mark (per D5)
